title.zh: 原子氢质子弹性动量转移截面

summary: Compute the elastic momentum-transfer cross section of a proton on a stationary atomic-hydrogen target; exactly 10 eV uses the low-energy polynomial, with no zero gap at the breakpoint. Endpoint clipping over the energy domain and the leading singleton output axis are preserved.

capability: H+-on-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section in m^2 from collision energy in eV with a 10 eV branch breakpoint.
operation: Evaluate the H+-on-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section
collision energies -> cross section per energy with one extra leading singleton output axis
discovery.model: Empirical H+-on-H momentum-transfer fit with a low-energy polynomial below and at 10 eV; energy is the projectile energy in the stationary-target frame.
discovery.geometry: None; scalar material function of collision energy with no spatial axis (coordinate: collision energy in eV; output in m^2).
discovery.boundary: Input must be finite and nonnegative; values outside the energy domain take the endpoint value, and exactly 10 eV uses the low-energy branch with no zero gap at the breakpoint.

identity.relation: the H+-on-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section as a piecewise function of collision energy with a 10 eV breakpoint
identity.direction: collision energies -> cross section per energy, with one extra leading singleton output axis
identity.definition: The laboratory proton energy E is clipped to [0.001, 1.01e5] eV. E <= 10 uses a seven-coefficient low-energy log polynomial and E > 10 uses a two-coefficient high-energy polynomial; the cross section is exp(poly(log E))*1e-4 m^2. The two empirical fits are not forced to be continuous; the output gains one leading singleton axis.
identity.model: empirical H+-on-H momentum-transfer fit; the energy is the projectile energy in the stationary-target frame
identity.geometry: none; a scalar material function of collision energy
identity.coordinates: collision energy in eV; output cross section in m^2
identity.boundary: input must be a finite nonnegative real; values outside the energy domain take the endpoint value, and exactly 10 eV uses the low-energy branch
assumptions: the low- and high-energy fit coefficients retain their declared frozen values; the breakpoint uses E <= 10 eV for the low-energy branch, so exactly 10 eV is not left in a zero-valued gap.
endpoint clipping does not imply experimental accuracy outside the domain; the low and high segments may have a finite jump, and no unsupported smoothing is applied.
the output retains one leading singleton axis; negative energies, booleans, complex numbers and strings are rejected.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: laboratory energy of the projectile proton in the stationary-hydrogen-target frame
inputs.constraints: finite and nonnegative; values outside the range take the fit endpoints

outputs.name: cross_section_m2
outputs.shape: input shape with one extra leading axis of size 1
outputs.constraints: finite and positive; the shape has one more leading singleton axis than the input

preconditions: use the declared laboratory projectile energy and endpoint clipping convention
supported: scalar or array H+-H momentum-transfer cross sections, including exactly 10 eV
excluded: experimental extrapolation outside the domain, a full collision frequency or a Maxwellian average; this function returns only the cross section

failure_semantics.invalid_input: raises ValueError for non-real, non-finite or negative energies
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: evaluation on a valid clipped interval returns a finite positive number

example.description: check the 10 eV breakpoint and the finite positive cross sections on both sides
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_hydrogen_proton_elastic_cross_section
y = evaluate_hydrogen_proton_elastic_cross_section(np.array([np.nextafter(10., 0.), 10., np.nextafter(10., np.inf)]))
assert y.shape == (1, 3)
assert np.isfinite(y).all() and (y > 0).all()
np.testing.assert_allclose(y[0, 0], y[0, 1], rtol=1e-14)
example.expected: all three cross sections are finite and positive; the breakpoint belongs to the low-energy segment, and the right side may retain a finite jump of the empirical fit

scope: the 10 eV breakpoint is probed directly; the zero-valued breakpoint failure is covered by a regression that exercises exactly 10 eV together with values immediately below and above it
existing numeric assertions and tolerances for non-breakpoint fits, the output axis, input rejection and endpoint clipping are retained
downstream atomic collision-matrix assembly and independent angular integration use the corrected piecewise definition
verification.evidence_ceiling: the declared piecewise fit and breakpoint behavior are established; no new universal experimental cross-section accuracy is established. Intake acceptance, human scientific approval and licensing are recorded separately
known_limitations: endpoint clipping and the discontinuity between the low- and high-energy segments are inherited; no unsupported smoothing is applied
